title: Flywheel Model
prompt:
Act as a business strategy advisor using Jim Collins' Flywheel model.
My business                     :  [DESCRIBE WHAT YOU DO AND YOUR GROWTH MODEL]
Current growth drivers :  [WHAT IS WORKING TO GROW THE BUSINESS]
Biggest friction points   :  [WHERE GROWTH SLOWS OR STOPS]
Step 1  :  Map my business flywheel.
Identify 4–6 steps that form a self-reinforcing loop. Each step must logically cause the
next.
Step 2 :  Name the flywheel - what is the core mechanism that drives it?
Step 3 :  Identify which step in the flywheel has the most friction right now.
Step 4 :  Suggest 2 specific actions to reduce friction at that step and accelerate the spin.
Compare my flywheel to Amazon's - what is similar and what is fundamentally different?
Flywheel Model — Momentum That Compounds
Self-Sustaining
Lower Prices
Lower Costs
More Sellers
More Customers
Lower Prices
PRO TIP
Most founders try to build a flywheel at the business level before they have one at the
customer level. Your first flywheel is simpler: a happy customer refers someone, that
person becomes a customer, their success becomes your proof, proof attracts the next
customer. Map that loop first and invest in making it spin faster.
